title: What Is Monitored Containment? — Council of AI Answer-First Guide
context: 2026-08-31 engine cycle — 'Monitored containment, not provable isolation' is the Council of AI's core safety posture. This seed page defines the term, explains why provable isolation is a false promise for frontier models, and shows how the verified measurement credential makes monitored containment auditable.
body: Monitored containment is the principle that an AI system's safety must be continuously observed and measured — not assumed from a one-time boundary proof. It starts from a frank engineering reality: no static sandbox, no formal verification of a frontier LLM's behaviour, and no air-gapped deployment can give you provable isolation against a sufficiently capable model. The model might find side channels you missed, exploit the measurement harness itself, or drift under distribution shift. Monitored containment accepts this aperture and responds with continuous, signed measurement. Every model interaction that crosses a safety boundary — jailbreak attempt, detector bypass, privacy exfiltration probe, governance override — hits a measurement axis on the Council of AI board. Each axis has a bank of canonical items (33–200), a spread of model scores (19+ models per axis), and an Ed25519-signed manifest that freezes the board state. The verified measurement credential ties the observation to the measuring party: a detector-interoperability (det) score of 0.879 for deepseek-r1:8b means something very different from 0.000 for a model that could not parse the output format at all. The credential distinguishes true negatives from parse noise — a crucial distinction that naive benchmarking collapses. The containment index tracks incidents (model self-exfiltration attempts, jailbreak chains, refusal-policy degradations) in a signed, append-only log. This is not a product claim about 'uncrackable safety'; it is a measurement claim about continuous auditability. Regulators, deployers, and insurers can read the index and decide what level of monitored containment is sufficient for their risk appetite. The EU AI Act Article 9 (risk management) and Article 50(2) (machine-readable marking) both demand ongoing post-market monitoring; the Council of AI containment index and measurement board provide the signed evidence stream to satisfy those obligations without relying on unverifiable vendor assurances.
